title: Personal Credit Cards: Closing a Card Account
content:
Closing an account on Personal Credit Cards is a decision that belongs to the cardholder. An active or a suspended card can be closed at the cardholder's own confirmed wish; a charged-off card is closed by the bank itself.

## Effects of closing

- An outstanding balance is no obstacle to closing. It stays payable on the terms already in place, minimum payments included, and any automatic payment keeps running until the balance has come down to zero.
- Points not yet redeemed are forfeited when the account closes.
- Where the annual fee posted within its refund window, it is taken back as the annual fee terms provide.
- On a Secured Visa, the security deposit is returned once the balance has been paid off completely.
- Money the bank owes the cardholder on a closed card, that is a credit balance, is paid back either as an official check or into a PCB account belonging to the customer.
- A closed account is never reopened; a customer who wants a card again makes a new application.

## Retired wording on how a closure is recorded

The former wording under which the agent registered a separate closure request awaiting the cardholder's confirmation, with the account closing only once that confirmation came in, is no longer in force. It has been superseded by the current closure basis, and it is kept on this page only so that the earlier practice is not mistaken for current rule.

## Basis Q&A

- **Must the balance be cleared before a card can be closed?** No; the balance survives the closure and remains owed.
- **Does automatic payment stop at closure?** Not while money is owed; it carries on until the balance reaches zero.
- **Can a closed card be brought back?** No; a fresh application is required.

superseded_clauses: the agent registers a card_requests row of request_type account_closure in pending_customer_confirmation status, and the account closes only after the cardholder confirms
